meta.name: Gantry Card Layout — shipped macOS values
meta.note: Exact values as implemented on macOS. Authority for the Windows/Linux port and enforced by scripts/check_ui_parity.py. Where this disagrees with gantry-design-tokens.json (0.2.0), this file wins.

zone.layout: horizontal, icon + current + smaller target on one line

statusColorContract.card: always accent (neutral); state read from text + icon
statusColorContract.listRow: neutral; error -> statusPrinting on icon + wash 0.08; stale -> systemOrange

settingsWindow.note: One design on all three platforms, each drawn by its own system's widgets. The card design with a pill tab bar is gone: it was the thing that made the window look like an app pretending to be a preferences window.

chrome.macOS: NSTabViewController tabStyle .toolbar inside a close-only title bar, NSWindow.toolbarStyle .preference
chrome.windows: SingleBorderWindow so the system title bar, immersive dark mode and rounded corners apply, a ListBox sidebar, SizeToContent Height
chrome.linux: Gtk.Dialog with use_header_bar, Gtk.StackSidebar over a non-homogeneous Gtk.Stack

settingsWindow.title: the active pane's name, so the Window menu reads correctly too
settingsWindow.layout: one two-column grid per pane: captions trailing in column 0, controls leading in column 1, one shared vertical axis down the whole window
settingsWindow.booleans: checkbox under a right-aligned category caption, not a switch row
settingsWindow.sections: a system separator plus a 13 pt semibold heading spanning both columns
settingsWindow.colors: system only: labelColor, secondaryLabelColor, the window's own material
settingsWindow.sizing: the window fits the active pane and carries no fixed size; the top edge stays put while the bottom moves

panelWindow.note: One frame for every panel window on all three platforms. Each is a window of its own, centred on the screen, wearing the fleet panel's own header so the family reads as one app. The panels no longer draw a title or a close button of their own.

staysEmbedded.onboarding guide: it points at the live cards behind it and dims them on purpose
staysEmbedded.startup overlay: it is the fleet panel's own loading state, not a panel
staysEmbedded.quick stock stepper: 190 points, anchored to the roll it adjusts inside the Spoolbase window
staysEmbedded.printer details and skip objects: navigation, not a modal: a page inside the fleet panel with a back button to the cards, so it keeps one window per fleet instead of one per printer

chrome.macOS: PanelWindowController: NSWindow [.titled, .closable, .resizable], titleVisibility .hidden and a transparent title bar, the same frame as the other nine windows; Escape closes via cancelOperation
chrome.windows: PanelWindow: a WPF Window with the system title bar, WindowStartupLocation CenterScreen, ShowInTaskbar false, Escape closes; panels that were already Windows are simply no longer re-hosted as overlays, and a wrapper ScrollViewer is opt-in so content with its own is not nested inside a second one
chrome.linux: PanelWindow: a Gtk.Window with a HeaderBar and a close button, Gtk.WindowPosition.CENTER, Escape closes; panels that were already Gtk.Dialogs stay dialogs and are simply no longer re-hosted as overlays

panelWindow.position: centred on the screen, not on the fleet panel, so it never opens on top of the cards

fleetPanelStaysOpen.rule: the fleet panel must remain visible and live while any panel is on screen
fleetPanelStaysOpen.macOS: the popover's behavior is switched from .transient to .applicationDefined and the outside-click monitor is suspended; a reference count, not a flag, so closing one of two open panels does not hand the popover back to AppKit
fleetPanelStaysOpen.windows: the dashboard's Deactivated handler walks OwnedWindows and returns while any is visible, so every panel must set Owner; inherently counted, unlike the macOS and Linux flags
fleetPanelStaysOpen.linux: Dashboard._suppress_hide is a reference count behind a property, held while any panel window is mapped, so the tray panel's focus-out hide cannot fire under it

maintenance.height: measured, and also the window's minimum so it cannot clip

slotAssignment.note: content below the header; Windows passes the outer 760x600

panelWindow.clamp: never wider or taller than the screen's visible frame less 40 points

header.content: GANTRY wordmark, a muted middle dot, the panel's name; the panel's own controls at the trailing end
header.separator: · (a middle dot, as in the fleet header; never a dash)

placement.macOS: in a unified compact title bar beside the traffic lights: an empty NSToolbar with toolbarStyle .unifiedCompact, fullSizeContentView, header height measured from the title bar (38 pt), wordmark leading 78 pt on the traffic lights' centre line, 1 pt line under it
placement.windows: a strip directly under the system title bar: Padding 16,9,12,9, MinHeight 44, 1 px Line border at the bottom; the system title bar shows the window title
placement.linux: the window's Gtk.HeaderBar itself: identity packed at the start, accessories at the end, an empty custom title so GTK draws no centred title, system close button

header.name: 13 pt semibold (Windows 14), text colour, truncates before the accessories

panelWindow.body: below the header, card colour, the panel's own content inset 16 to 18; close is the system button or Escape

slotAssignment.layout: two equal columns on the main screen: left = the slot (material, assigned roll and its actions, spare rolls); right = create a new roll and the filament catalogue; each column scrolls its own list
slotAssignment.why: one column stacked everything into a window 460x640, more than twice as tall as wide
slotAssignment.singleColumnScreens: weigh, pick a filament, starting amount: one column, centred, at most singleColumnWidth wide
slotAssignment.linux: the Gtk.Dialog content area holds the same two columns: the assigned roll on the left, the roll picker on the right

edgeDock.note: The always-on-top strip at a screen edge. One behaviour on all three platforms: a pin on the strip both pins and releases it, and any printer can have a live picture under its own row (issue #34).

pinControl.shape: a pushpin upright with the needle down: flat head, shaft, flared collar, needle
pinControl.released: hollow outline in the secondary colour, stroke 1.3/16 of the glyph, leaning over by releasedAngle
pinControl.pinned: filled in the text colour, standing straight (0 degrees)
pinControl.rotation: clockwise as seen on screen; design box is y-down, macOS flips y when placing points
pinControl.placement: in the ring column, in a band above the first row, present whenever the strip is open
pinControl.action: click toggles edge-dock-pinned; hover lifts the disc (and shows a hand cursor on Windows); tooltip Keep the strip open
pinControl.rendering: a vector path on every platform, never an emoji or a platform symbol, so it is the same shape everywhere

cameras.choice: printers ticked in Settings; with none ticked, the printing (then paused) printer, or the only candidate
cameras.streams: restarted only when the set of printers changes; kept running while folded; stopped when the strip hides
cameras.placeholder: a dark plate until the first frame
cameras.hitTest: a click on a picture does not open details

edgeDock.ringPlacement: the ring stays beside the physical screen edge while the text unfolds inward

capsule.layout: one inset capsule [ minus | caption value | plus ] with hairline separators; flat ends with hover and pressed fills

detailControls.values: snapped to the step grid; a heater target of 0 reads as off; the command goes out once the value settles and a pending one is sent when the view closes
detailControls.temperatureTiles: the capsule sits inside the nozzle and bed tiles and carries the target; the tile reads the live temperature; all three readings share one size and line
detailControls.fanTiles: two to a row; Klipper shows part fan and speed only; the read-only gauges are hidden while the tiles show
detailControls.advanced: Advanced… sits on the camera card header, clear of the drag grip
